mappings.note: Pure terminology: what the principal focus IS. No outcome defines mirror parts; the competency is the one that names focus and centre of curvature as the properties being handled. Not LO-1, which is about stating reflection laws and locating an image.
f = R/2 numerical. The mirror-formula outcome owns the f-R relation; LO-1 would be wrong because no image is located here.
Names the mirror from a stated image character (erect, magnified) - that is characterising the image of a concave mirror, not a formula computation.
Convex mirror always gives an erect diminished image with a wide field; the reasoning is image character, not the mirror formula.
f = R/2 arithmetic for a convex mirror; no image is located, so LO-2 and not LO-1.
Magnification formula m = -v/u with m = -3 and u = -10 to get v. Squarely the magnification-formula outcome, not the qualitative image outcome.
Air-to-water bending is the law of refraction plus optical density; LO-3 is the refraction outcome.
Speed of light from refractive index. Refraction outcome, which explicitly covers defining refractive index.
Definition of the dioptre. Power of a lens appears in no learning outcome; the competency names lens properties, so it rests there.
P = 1/f for a lens. Power reaches no outcome - LO-3 covers the lens FORMULA, not lens power - so it sits at the competency.
Tests that a lens must be transparent; neither the refraction laws nor the lens formula is used, so it stays at the competency.
Virtual, erect, enlarged from a concave mirror means the object is inside the focus; a qualitative image-location judgement, so LO-1 not LO-2.
Real same-size image from a convex lens fixes the object at 2F; the lens image-position outcome, not the mirror outcome.
Entirely about reading f = -15 cm: negative f means a concave mirror but a concave lens. That is the Cartesian sign convention, not a formula application.
Always-erect image for every object distance identifies plane or convex mirror; qualitative mirror image outcome.
Choice turns on which lens has greater magnifying strength (shorter focal length), i.e. lens power, which no outcome names.
Two things are demanded: the object range for an erect image in a concave mirror (LO-1) and an explicitly drawn ray diagram (C 8.1-LO-2). The drawing is required, not incidental.
Matches three applications to mirror types by the image each forms; the mirror image-character outcome, not any formula.
About image completeness and brightness when part of the aperture is blocked. Neither the refraction laws nor the lens formula answers it, so competency level.
Lens formula to get position, size and nature (LO-3) plus an explicitly required ray diagram (C 8.1-LO-2).
Mirror formula with f = +15 cm, u = -10 cm. A calculation, so LO-2 rather than the qualitative convex-mirror outcome.
m = +1 is read through the magnification formula (LO-2) and the whole content is what the PLUS sign means, which is the sign convention (C 5.3-LO-1).
Convex mirror, R given, needs f = R/2 then the mirror and magnification formulae. A calculation item.
Concave mirror numerical: screen distance is v from the mirror formula, size from magnification. LO-2, not the qualitative LO-1.
Two distinct steps: f = 1/P, which is lens power and reaches no outcome (competency), and the minus sign identifying a concave lens (sign convention).
Same pair as the -2.0 D item: power-to-focal-length (competency) plus the plus sign showing a converging lens (sign convention).
Uses the lens formula relation between u and v to decide which way the screen moves and how m changes. Lens image-position outcome.
Completing an incomplete lens ray diagram is the ray-diagram outcome; identifying the object position from it is the lens image-position outcome. Figure not stored.
Tracks how the lens image distance and size change as the object approaches; the lens image-position outcome, done without a required drawing.
Object position for a virtual image from a convex lens (LO-3) and an explicitly demanded ray diagram (C 8.1-LO-2).
Candle-and-screen sequence for a convex lens: how v, size and intensity vary with u. Lens image-position outcome; no drawing is asked for.
Same convex-lens screen sequence including the same-size distance at 2F. Lens image-position outcome.
Always-virtual, always-erect for every object position identifies a convex mirror; qualitative mirror image outcome.
Reads optical density off refractive-index values; the refraction outcome explicitly covers refractive index. Table is not stored with the stem.
Compares speed of light through refractive index values; refraction outcome.
Speed maxima/minima plus a relative refractive index calculation; refraction outcome. Table not stored.
Picks medium pairs where light speeds up or slows down, straight from refractive index; refraction outcome. Table not stored.
The bent pencil is refraction at the water surface with an apparent-position shift; a refraction item, not a mirror or lens ray diagram, so not C 8.1-LO-2.
Deliberately spans both elements: a source at the focus of a concave mirror (LO-1) and of a convex lens (LO-3) both give a parallel beam. Both are needed to eliminate the distractors.
Magnification from object and image heights, then the mirror formula for f. A calculation, so LO-2.
Real image larger than the object means the object is between F and C of a concave mirror; qualitative image-position judgement.
Compares bending at an A-to-B boundary to decide whether the relative refractive index exceeds one; refraction outcome. Figure not stored.
Identifies the optical element purely from the drawn ray paths in and out of the box; that is reading a mirror/lens ray diagram. Figure not stored.
Same box-and-rays construction: the element is inferred from the drawn ray paths. Figure not stored.
Tests the P = 1/f arithmetic (competency, since power reaches no outcome) together with which sign goes with which lens (sign convention).
Phrased in terms of the magnification VALUE being less than one, so the magnification-formula outcome rather than the qualitative image outcome.
Sun rays converging at 15 cm fixes f, then a same-size image requires the object at C = 2f = 30 cm. Uses f and the magnification condition, so LO-2.
Only a convex mirror gives a full-length diminished image of a tall building; qualitative mirror image outcome.
Bulb at the focus of a concave reflector gives a parallel beam; a mirror image-position fact, not a formula.
Directly asks the scope of the laws of reflection, which is the first clause of LO-1.
Correct path through a rectangular glass slab is refraction at two parallel faces. Not a mirror or lens diagram, so LO-3 rather than C 8.1-LO-2.
Which medium bends the ray most is decided by refractive index; refraction outcome.
Chooses the correct reflected ray for a concave mirror: the standard mirror construction rays, which is the ray-diagram outcome. Figure not stored.
Chooses the correct refracted ray for a lens: the standard lens construction rays. Figure not stored.
Magic-mirror strip requires knowing which mirror enlarges, keeps size, and diminishes; qualitative mirror image outcome.
The options deliberately mix mirrors and lenses, so both the mirror image outcome and the lens image outcome are needed to reject the single-element distractors.
Four cases split between mirrors and lenses; identifying each device needs both the mirror and the lens image-position outcomes.
Emergent ray parallel after a slab is refraction at two parallel faces; a refraction proof, not a mirror/lens ray diagram.
Extent of apparent bending varies with the liquid's refractive index; refraction outcome.
Asks for refractive index in terms of speed and derives the relative refractive index; the definition clause of LO-3.
Object positions of a convex lens for a magnified real and a magnified virtual image; lens image-position outcome.
Truncated stem, but it is the distant-building convex-lens item: which way the screen moves and the approximate focal length. Lens image-position outcome.
P = 1/f and choosing the more convergent lens by focal length. Lens power reaches no outcome, so competency level.
Two plane mirrors at 90 degrees keep the emergent ray antiparallel; the reasoning is the law of reflection applied twice, so LO-1 rather than the mirror/lens ray-diagram outcome.
Drawing the bending of a ray at an air-water boundary is refraction, not a mirror or lens ray diagram, so LO-3 not C 8.1-LO-2.
Science content is that a convex lens concentrates sunlight at its focus; a lens property, not the lens formula. The values part reaches no outcome at all.
Shop surveillance mirrors are convex because of the wide erect field; qualitative mirror image outcome.
Distorted funhouse image from curved mirror sections; qualitative mirror image outcome.
Telescope lenses. The competency explicitly extends to a COMBINATION of lenses (telescope, microscope); no outcome covers it.
Definition of reflection, the phenomenon LO-1 opens with.
A reflector is a surface used to reflect light; belongs with the reflection outcome.
Literally the first clause of LO-1: states the laws of reflection.
Normal incidence gives i = r = 0, a direct application of the law of reflection.
General image vocabulary that applies to mirrors AND lenses alike; LO-1 is mirror-specific, so this rests at the competency.
Same reason as the real-image definition: image vocabulary spanning both mirrors and lenses.
Nature of a plane-mirror image is exactly what LO-1 asks the learner to locate and characterise.
Mirror geometry terminology. The competency names centre of curvature as a property being handled; no outcome defines it.
Mirror geometry terminology, same treatment as centre of curvature.
Aperture is pure mirror geometry; no outcome mentions it.
Pole is pure mirror geometry; no outcome mentions it.
Principal axis is pure mirror geometry; no outcome mentions it.
Definition of the principal focus of a convex mirror, handled the same as the concave-mirror focus definition: terminology at competency level.
Focal length defined as the pole-to-focus distance is geometry; the f-R RELATION (LO-2) is a different item.
f = R/2 is the relation the mirror formula work rests on, so the mirror-formula outcome.
Converging and diverging mirrors named from how they treat light; the reflection/image outcome.
Always erect and diminished for every object position identifies the convex mirror; qualitative image outcome.
Real same-size image from a concave mirror puts the object at C; qualitative image-position judgement with no formula.
Magnified virtual image needs the object between P and F; qualitative image-position judgement.
Image of any object in a convex mirror lies between P and F behind the mirror; qualitative image location.
Names the mirror from a stated image character; qualitative image outcome.
Asks for the mirror formula itself, which is the opening clause of LO-2.
Definition of linear magnification, the second formula named in LO-2.
Magnification of a plane mirror is +1 because the image and object distances are equal; a magnification-formula item.
Dentist's mirror is concave because it gives an erect magnified image of a near object; qualitative image outcome.
Rear-view mirror is convex for the erect diminished wide-field image; qualitative image outcome.
Headlight reflector is concave with the bulb at the focus; mirror image/application outcome.
Solar furnace uses a large concave mirror to converge sunlight; mirror image/application outcome.
A ray through C hits the mirror along the normal, so i = 0 and it retraces. Pure law of reflection.
Shop surveillance mirrors are convex for the wide field; mirror application outcome.
Explicitly asks the candidate to DRAW the ray diagram for a given object in front of a concave mirror; that is the ray-diagram outcome.
Definition of refraction, the phenomenon LO-3 opens with.
Cause of refraction is the change in speed between media; refraction outcome.
Defines and expresses absolute refractive index, which LO-3 names explicitly.
Relative refractive index definition; LO-3 covers defining refractive index.
Snell's law IS the law of refraction named in LO-3.
Why light bends at a boundary: change of speed. Refraction outcome.
Absolute refractive index exceeds one because light is fastest in vacuum; refraction outcome.
Frequency is unchanged across a boundary while speed and wavelength change; a refraction fact.
Normal incidence at a boundary gives no bending; a refraction item despite the concept tag saying reflection.
Incident and emergent rays through a slab are parallel, so the angle between them is zero; refraction through a slab.
Lateral displacement is defined for a ray refracted through a slab; refraction outcome.
Optical centre is lens geometry terminology; no outcome defines lens parts.
Principal axis of a lens is geometry terminology, treated like the mirror equivalents.
Definition of the principal focus of a convex lens; terminology, so competency level, matching the mirror focus definitions.
Definition of the principal focus of a concave lens; terminology at competency level.
Focal length of a lens defined as the optical-centre-to-focus distance; terminology.
Names the lens purely from the drawn incident and refracted rays; reading a lens ray diagram. Figure not stored.
Same construction as the companion item: the lens is identified from the drawn ray path. Figure not stored.
Asks what a negative image distance SIGNIFIES under the Cartesian convention; the sign-convention outcome, not the lens formula.
Defines power of a lens and the dioptre; power appears in no outcome, so competency level.
